name: Nothern Cape
summary_text: The single documented trans-specific violent incident in this dossier occurred here: on 14 May 2024 in Upington, 27-year-old transgender woman Jo-Ann Isaks was stabbed multiple times and her body set on fire in her own room, discovered by a family member who noticed the house burning. TGEU's Trans Day of Remembrance register records the killing and notes that "the LGBTIQ+ community in the Northern Cape has been shaken" - a province-level community response in a small province where one violent death is a meaningful rate observation. Police opened a murder case and reported no arrests at the time of the entry; the register records that police 'identified' the decedent by a deadname. The killing is a lone incident and not clearly patterned or state-implicated; there is no evidence of impunity or victim-prosecution in the dossier, and no provincial legislative or enforcement finding against trans visitors. The score therefore reflects severity-dominant weighting: the method (burning) is extreme and the community-level shock signal is real, but the single-incident rule cautions against large score moves from an unpatterned crime. Northern Cape does not appear in the customary-authority / traditional-court geography and has no identified institutional climate finding. The score is 0.05 below the national 0.69. vs. Gauteng (0.71) and Western Cape (0.72), the gap is driven by a concrete trans-identified murder and the small-population rate effect rather than by any jurisdictional or legislative divergence. vs. Mpumalanga (0.65) and Limpopo (0.65), the Northern Cape sits at a similar level: Mpumalanga/Limpopo carry diffuse institutional-climate and jurisdictional risk without a single trans-specific incident, whereas Northern Cape has one severe incident without patterned institutional backing. The dossier's under-reporting caveat means other provinces may experience similar violence without it reaching TGEU's register.

sources.title: Remembering Our Dead - Jo-Ann Isaks (14 May 2024)
sources.claim_summary: TGEU Trans Day of Remembrance register entry (14 May 2024): Jo-Ann Isaks, 27, a transgender woman, was found dead in a burning room in the Paballelo location of Upington after multiple stab wounds; a family member noticed the fire at about 23:00. Police (ZF Mgcawu District) confirmed a murder case, with no arrests at the time of the entry, and referred to the decedent by a deadname; the entry quotes district LGBTIQ+ leader Jenny Sambok and reports the province's LGBTIQ+ community 'shaken'.
